context.preamble: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
context.what-this-is: This is a crate called 'enforcer' that does various checks on a Rust codebase. Each check is a set of rules. The enforcer runs that check telling you if your codebase has any violations.

cargo-commands.test: There is no test suite at the moment. Don't add tests unless asked.
cargo-commands.enforcer: cargo run enforcer all - To run the enforcer itself on its own code
cargo-commands.notes: `cargo clippy` and `cargo run enforcer all` should be run after each change to make sure there are no warnings. However, leave any new enforcer violations introduced from your change alone, so that I can see them.

rust-code-preferences.private-fns: Whenever defining private functions/methods (i.e. without 'pub'), start the function/method name with an underscore.

enforcer-import-rules.general-guide: The idea is to put all static data in 's' dirs and public types in 't' dirs. There can also be some basic impl's for simple methods in the 't' directories alongside the types. 'ext_traits' are for extension traits (adding traits to types we don't own). Principle: minimize c (ideally nothing in it), instead placing code as deep as possible, right where it's used. However, a balancing principle: extract duplicated logic to 'c' dirs. Principle: put all types used multiple places in 't' directories.
